Use case: style-transfer. User-requested setting concept for actual Unity game physics map Canopy Borough: "Inside the Honeycomb". Input1 is the actual whole-map reference with all structures; Input2 a closer construction reference. Preserve recognizable counts, locations, heights, floor holes, flat rectangular slabs, pillars, bridges, leaning/stepped forms and low open structures. User wants creative unique surfaces and sparse visual objects, and has rejected uniform skin packs and pretending abstract frames are literal skyscrapers/buildings.
Create ONE polished high-resolution LANDSCAPE concept board. Main immersive whole-map scene fills left 75%, close-up strip of THREE tactile material / ornament detail insets fills right 25%. Short title at top "Inside the Honeycomb". Main composition recognizable from Input1, crop empty sky, include surroundings to make the setting unmistakable. Add 3 short restrained callout arrows in main scene showing HOW ORIGINAL STRUCTURAL SHAPES got different materials; labels describe material or ornament only. Strong playful polished Unity candy/toy 3D art, achievable stylized surface language, not photographic. Depth and light are beautiful but all open routes clearly readable.
EXACT SETTING AND SURFACE DIRECTION: The actual map sits ON the floor of a colossal honeycomb beehive, fully surrounded by distant curved golden wax cell walls and softly backlit translucent amber honeycomb ceiling. Outside scenery not tropical ocean: distant honey-colored void/shimmer beyond the map's playable edge, clearly boundary-like. The island footprint is a slightly concave broad wax floor. The actual branching crown slabs KEEP their rectangular outlines and holes, but show BIG hexagonal cell textures on wax sides; opaque pale buttery walkable tops, amber gilled undersides. Use different wax families by structure: center crown rich golden-orange and dark rough wooden posts, west pale beeswax with pollen yellow, east smoky amber resin with near-black posts, tall skinny skyline deep brown glossy propolis sides with cream tops. Low courtyards and folded pavilions pale wax with small attached patches of hexagonal comb on OUTSIDE corners; a few slow bees nearby, tiny pollen clusters and restrained short thick honey drips underneath external lips. Never put honey obstacles on walking tops. No replacing rectangular decks by hexagonal platforms, no new traversable structures. Cozy magical macro scale, rich toy-like wax translucency only on side accents, warm light through cell walls with enough fill to read voids. Bees tiny relative structures, no swarm clutter.
Contrast different structural families WITHIN the same map. Walkable tops opaque, quiet and readable; expressive grain/gills/cells/strata on sides and undersides. Sparse small embellishments on exterior edges and post backs only, designed as visual children of original pieces. No new walls, towers or occupied passage gaps. Large environment-setting forms may exist outside/below the gameplay footprint as BACKDROP art as specified; do not replace individual structures by props. Preserve original abstract geometry as the core of the image; do not just draw a generic theme park or jungle scene. Footer "AI SETTING CONCEPT • ORIGINAL MAP SHAPES AS REFERENCE • NOT UNITY CAPTURE".
